## What it is

Hermes Agent is Nous Research's open-source (MIT) AI agent. It keeps a memory of you across sessions, writes and improves its own skills, runs scheduled tasks, and can be reached from chat apps (Telegram, Discord, Slack and others) through one gateway process. It works with many model providers (OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, Nous Portal, local endpoints). Source: the upstream [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/v0.23.0/README.md).

On OneMind it is the first founder app (contract `sdk/contracts/poc-v0.md` §7). It proves the core rule end to end: **an AI agent requests, a human approves, the OS executes.** At install the gateway gives Hermes its own agent identity, `agent:hermes-agent`. Hermes can read nodes and apps and *request* actions through the gateway's MCP endpoint. It has no way to approve them (§3, §11.3).

## How it is packaged

- **Image:** `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.23.0`, pinned by the index digest named in contract §7 (amd64 and arm64). One container runs `gateway run` under the image's own s6-overlay supervisor, plus the web dashboard (`HERMES_DASHBOARD=true`, port 9119, the app's web port). The API server listens on 8642 for the `GET /health` probes and is not in the Service.
- **Non-root:** the image starts as root only so it can remap its `hermes` user (UID 10000). Upstream supports starting directly as that UID ([docker/stage2-hook.sh](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/v0.23.0/docker/stage2-hook.sh)), so the pod runs as 10000:10000 with every capability dropped and no privilege escalation. s6-overlay needs a `/run` owned by that UID. An init container creates one in a pod-local `emptyDir`.
- **State:** `HERMES_HOME=/opt/data` on the 5Gi PVC `hermes-agent-data`, holding config, `.env`, sessions, memories, skills and logs. The Deployment uses the `Recreate` strategy, so only one pod ever writes it.
- **First-boot config:** the init container `seed-config` (`manifests/seed/seed.py`) writes `config.yaml` once. It contains Hermes's own example config plus:
  - one MCP server, `mcp_servers.onemind` → `${ONEMIND_GATEWAY_URL}/mcp` with `Authorization: Bearer ${ONEMIND_AGENT_TOKEN}`. Hermes expands `${VAR}` from its environment ([MCP docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/mcp)).
  - a dashboard login, user `owner`, with a random password. Only its scrypt hash goes into `config.yaml`; the plaintext is in `/opt/data/onemind-dashboard-password`, mode 0600.

  After that the file is the owner's, and the seed never rewrites it.
- **Secrets, never in this repo:**
  - `hermes-agent-onemind` (required): `ONEMIND_GATEWAY_URL` and `ONEMIND_AGENT_TOKEN`. The gateway creates it at install (§11.2) and deletes it on removal.
  - `hermes-agent-credentials`: the owner's model-provider keys, declared in `spec.secrets`. The owner types them into the install approval; the gateway stores them encrypted with the box's key and writes this Secret before Hermes starts ([SECRETS.md](../../docs/leap/core/SECRETS.md)). The Deployment loads it as environment variables and marks it optional, so the pod also starts before a key is set.
- **API server key:** on first boot the image's bootstrap generates `API_SERVER_KEY` into `/opt/data/.env`.

## First run

The last scan of this image failed (see below), so the gateway refuses to install it until a scan passes. A box owner who accepts the findings can turn on the F-7 owner override (`ONEMIND_ALLOW_OWNER_OVERRIDE=1`, off by default) and approve the install with a typed confirmation and a reason; the audit log then carries a red `owner override: <reason>` mark ([DECISIONS-NEEDED F-7](../../docs/leap/DECISIONS-NEEDED.md)).

1. **Enter your model key while approving the install.** The approval card shows a form for `hermes-agent-credentials`: an OpenRouter, Anthropic or OpenAI key, and optionally an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Fill in the provider you use. The browser encrypts the form to the box's key, so the key never travels or rests in plain text, and no shell command is needed. To change or rotate it later, use the app's Secrets panel (`POST /v1/apps/hermes-agent/secrets`), which files a change you approve like any other; Hermes restarts with the new value.

   Other providers Hermes supports (listed in its [`.env.example`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/v0.23.0/.env.example)) need a manifest change that declares their variable first.

2. **Open the dashboard:** `kubectl -n app-hermes-agent port-forward svc/hermes-agent 9119:9119`, then go to <http://localhost:9119>. Sign in as `owner` with the password from `kubectl -n app-hermes-agent exec deploy/hermes-agent -- cat /opt/data/onemind-dashboard-password`. Upstream warns that the dashboard can read and write your API keys: keep it on a trusted network ([dashboard docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard)).
3. **Pick a model:** in the dashboard, or with `kubectl -n app-hermes-agent exec -it deploy/hermes-agent -- hermes model` ([Docker docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/docker)).

## Demo: the agent asks, the owner approves (contract §7)

1. Install Hermes from the Market and approve it as the owner. The gateway creates `agent:hermes-agent` and the Secret `hermes-agent-onemind`. Then do the first-run steps above.
2. Ask Hermes to install ntfy, in the dashboard chat or from a shell:
   `kubectl -n app-hermes-agent exec deploy/hermes-agent -- hermes chat -q "Use the onemind tools to install the ntfy app"`.
   Hermes calls `request_action` (`app.install`, `app_id: ntfy`) on the gateway's MCP endpoint.
3. In the dashboard's **Approvals** screen, the action shows as `awaiting_approval`, requested by an agent. Hermes cannot approve it: there is no approve tool, and `POST /v1/actions/{id}/approve` returns 403 to an agent.
4. Approve it as the owner. ntfy is installed into `app-ntfy`. The audit chain records requester `agent:hermes-agent` and approver `person:owner`.
